newsitem.title: HUNGARY: PM says Hungary close to cracking bombing wave.
newsitem.headline: PM says Hungary close to cracking bombing wave.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn said on Tuesday that police had made a breakthrough in solving a wave of bombings in the biggest criminal investigation since he came to power in 1994.
"This could prove to be the turning point in both the bombing wave and in uncovering serious fraud," Horn told a news conference.

Last week, when announcing the arrests of 13 suspects, police said the bombings had been devised to divert their attention from fuel tax and excise duty evasion amounting to "billions of forints" (millions of dollars).
"The investigation is still going on but billions of forints were misappropriated," Horn said.
Police said earlier that almost two dozen explosions of grenades and petrol bombs, most of which have occurred in Budapest since September, were linked to an escalating gang turf war.

Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze told the news conference the fraud cases went back to the early 1990s when subsidised heating oil was sold as vehicle fuel, illegally raising tens of billions of forints.
Horn said police officers and top customs officials had been prosecuted in connection with the cases but added: "There is no indication that other state agencies are involved".
